alexanderbathfalamorthethird: The new signaller is Otto Alexanderbat, once a clockmaker from Marrow Fen. The corporal asked if a clockmaker was any use in a trench. Otto Alexanderbat said he would find out.

The corporal found out Otto Alexanderbat used to be a clockmaker. Otto Alexanderbat has been doing two jobs ever since. On Day 3, Verdel Ridge passed to the Concord. Otto Alexanderbat wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.
Otto Alexanderbat (Concord) and Cyril "Doc" Zaboravljeni (Hegemony) ended up in the same shell hole at Lantern Hill. They stared at each other. Then each crawled home, and neither has told anyone.
Edmund "Hollow" Biwott and Otto Alexanderbat tried to invent a new card game. The rules only made sense once they stopped betting tobacco.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. Machine-gun fire swept S-F8. Otto Alexanderbat took a round through the side and was carried back, grey in the face and very quiet. Mail came up the line with a letter for Otto Alexanderbat. Otto Alexanderbat read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. The sergeant read out the order: Hill 304 has fallen, hold the line. Otto Alexanderbat looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.
Otto Alexanderbat finally has a bed in the hospital dugout. A real blanket, a lamp, and a surgeon who has not slept.
Otto Alexanderbat spent the day in bed with his leg propped up. The orderly changed the dressing and said it was healing the way it should.
The medical officer cleared Otto Alexanderbat for duty. At S-F8, someone quietly moved a pack off his usual seat.
Otto Alexanderbat and Nils Photo carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident.
Blackwater Canal is in Hegemony hands. Otto Alexanderbat stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.

Otto Alexanderbat sent a pigeon back to headquarters. The pigeon came back two hours later. Otto Alexanderbat took it personally. Mail came up the line with a letter for Otto Alexanderbat. Otto Alexanderbat read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. Otto Alexanderbat got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 127. The men who came later will ask about it.
anthony.dagata: The new rifleman is Dietrich Dagata, once a ferryman from Lindenbruck. The corporal asked if a ferryman was any use in a trench. Dietrich Dagata said he would find out.

A parcel from home held a comb. Dietrich Dagata has hardly any hair left after the last haircut, but he appreciated the thought. A letter from home reached Dietrich Dagata before dusk. Dietrich Dagata read it twice and slept a little easier.
echoss_3: Day 5. The corporal put Gustav "Spark" Echoss beside a veteran and said to copy everything except the language.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. Gustav "Spark" Echoss tore his hands on the barbs and did not make a sound. The new wire at R-F2 is up. The sergeant read out the order: Hill 304 has fallen, hold the line. Gustav "Spark" Echoss looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.
Gustav "Spark" Echoss shaved using a spoon for a mirror. One side looks ready for inspection. The other looks ready for winter.
Gustav "Spark" Echoss tried to write neatly for the first line of a letter. By the third, he was writing as quickly as the thoughts arrived.
Gustav "Spark" Echoss swept the enemy parapet at R-F2 with one long burst. Dust jumped all along the sandbags. Benedikt Finland was badly wounded.
At the Sunken Road, Konrad "Whistle" Szymanski of the Hegemony and Gustav "Spark" Echoss of the Concord spent the morning shooting at the same loose sheet of metal. The sheet kept winning.

The Hegemony raiders were in and out in two minutes. At R-F2 they left Gustav "Spark" Echoss behind, dead on the duckboards. Killed in the night raid by Ivo "Rabbit" Beck of the Hegemony (@brandon_marc_beck).
Pavel "Ghost" Echoss had heard about Gustav "Spark" Echoss's courage. At R-F2, he also heard about the snoring, the cards and the terrible handwriting.

Officers came to inspect R-F2. Pavel "Ghost" Echoss polished his buttons with mud, which is the only polish there is. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Pavel "Ghost" Echoss is number 332. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech.
flyerz108: Tobias Flyerz unpacked a stub of a pencil at R-R5. The man in the next bunk shifted his bag to make room without asking what it was.
Tobias Flyerz walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
Tobias Flyerz bought a small phrasebook from a passing soldier. The first useful sentence appears after six pages about hiring a carriage.
jaranda543: On the way to V-F14, Wendel Jaranda tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way.
jewnipers: Lucien Jewnipers unpacked a cracked shaving mirror at R-F17. A neighbour shifted a bag to make room without asking what it was.
The sergeant read out the order: Verdel Ridge has fallen, hold the line. Lucien Jewnipers looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.

Lucien Jewnipers was hit through the chest at R-F17. He is breathing. That is all the medic would say. Shot by Quentin "Shadow" Danny of the Concord (@sus.danny2.0). An orderly waved the bearers in: one bed, cleared and scrubbed. Lucien Jewnipers was lifted onto it in the hospital dugout. Lucien Jewnipers slipped away in the night. The orderly who sat with him says he was not afraid.
Clement Jewnipers put a cracked shaving mirror beside the bunk. Someone who had known Lucien Jewnipers helped clear the shelf without saying why.

Clement Jewnipers fired at a movement across the wire at R-F17. The man went down: Ulrich Gpt, badly wounded. Clement Jewnipers raised his head for a heartbeat too long at R-F17. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Teodor Deanc of the Concord (@deanc_67).

Clement Jewnipers sat out the day with a bandaged arm, cleaning every rifle within reach. It was the only job the medic would allow. The Hegemony flag went up over Hill 304. Clement Jewnipers did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
Clement Jewnipers's bandage came off today. The scar is ugly. He is rather proud of it.
Viktor Newnario and Clement Jewnipers carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident.
On a quiet night Clement Jewnipers (Hegemony) and Norbert Bucket (Concord) called out their names across no man's land, just to hear another voice. Now each knows exactly who is out there.
A new recruit would not eat with the others. Clement Jewnipers left a place at the end of the bench and said nothing about it.

The Concord raiders came over at R-F17 in the middle of the night. Clement Jewnipers met them first and did not survive the fight. Killed in the night raid by Silas "Hollow" Jerebearmorr of the Concord (@jerebearmorrison).
The papers say Benedikt Jewnipers. The sergeant says he has his cousin's eyes. Clement Jewnipers's eyes. Nobody in R-F17 argues.

Benedikt Jewnipers woke with his hair frozen to the sandbags. The cook brought tea so hot it hurt. Nobody complained. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Benedikt Jewnipers answered to number 146.
majormalpractice_626: Nobody saw Emil Majormalprac arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in S-F5, and a quiet machine gunner under it.
Emil Majormalprac ended a letter with 'nothing to report', then added half a page about the missing soap.

Clement Tsanev taught Emil Majormalprac to play the harmonica. The whole squad has asked them both, politely, to stop. A letter from home found Emil Majormalprac before the night shift. Emil Majormalprac folded it small and kept it close.

Emil Majormalprac went out with the wiring party at S-F5. Crawl, hammer a stake, pull the wire, crawl back. Nobody was hit. A clear shot from S-F5. Emil Majormalprac badly wounded Leopold "Doc" Cornkkob and slid back down below the parapet. A letter from home found Emil Majormalprac before the night shift. Emil Majormalprac folded it small and kept it close. The Hegemony hold Hill 304 now, and they can see straight into S-F5. Emil Majormalprac has learned to walk bent double.

Emil Majormalprac had been watching the same gap for an hour. When Ulrich Pgallo crossed it, Emil Majormalprac fired. Ulrich Pgallo was grazed. A letter from home found Emil Majormalprac before the night shift. Emil Majormalprac folded it small and kept it close.
Emil Majormalprac cleaned the gun for the fourth time today. The gun is the only thing in the trench that is kept dry.
A dog crosses no man's land at Verdel Ridge every night, fed by Emil Majormalprac on one side and Valentin "Saint" Oliverjarret on the other. The Concord call it Patrol. The Hegemony call it Spy.

Emil Majormalprac had kept the gun aimed at the enemy supply path for days. Tonight the supply party came, and Albin Travismac was grazed. The gun at S-F5 jammed twice and fired once. Once was enough: Roland Monster, grazed. A letter from home found Emil Majormalprac before the night shift. Emil Majormalprac folded it small and kept it close.

Emil Majormalprac fired one burst and pulled the gun down before the reply came. The reply hit empty sandbags. Otto Dunkmyanactu did not get to reply at all, grazed. From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Emil Majormalprac wrote to a teacher who said he would amount to nothing that night and said only: 'We will take it back.' A letter from home found Emil Majormalprac before the night shift. Emil Majormalprac folded it small and kept it close.

A parcel from home held a comb. Emil Majormalprac has hardly any hair left after the last haircut, but he appreciated the thought. Emil Majormalprac got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 207. The men who came later will ask about it.
mateorekon: The quartermaster asked Cyril Mateorekon to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Cyril Mateorekon was number 78. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Cyril Mateorekon noticed regular flashes from a crack in an old stone wall. The position looks obvious enough to make him suspicious.

On sentry duty Cyril Mateorekon watched the wire for six hours. Twice he thought the wire watched back. The Concord hold Verdel Ridge now, and they can see straight into S-F9. Cyril Mateorekon has learned to walk bent double.
Cyril Mateorekon had been watching the same gap for an hour. When Nils Zczc crossed it, Cyril Mateorekon fired. Nils Zczc was grazed.
A shell burst in the trench at S-F9. Cyril Mateorekon was thrown against the wall and did not get up. The bearers came at a run.

Cyril Mateorekon drifted in and out on the stretcher. Every time he woke, the line for the beds seemed longer. The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Hill 304. Cyril Mateorekon folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
Every bed was taken and every medic was busy. Cyril Mateorekon died waiting. The men at S-F9 have not stopped talking about it.

Marek "Lucky" Mateorekon asked about Cyril Mateorekon on arriving at S-F9. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another. The First Wave ribbon marked Marek "Lucky" Mateorekon as an early volunteer. At S-F9, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.
Fog so thick that Marek "Lucky" Mateorekon could not see the end of his own rifle. Somewhere out there, someone was whistling.
Marek "Lucky" Mateorekon had marked the enemy's path to the latrine on a scrap of paper. Today it paid off: Wendel "Mole" Day, grazed.
A periscope poked up from the enemy line. Marek "Lucky" Mateorekon shot it to pieces, and the man holding it, Norbert Slc, was grazed.

Marek "Lucky" Mateorekon was on watch at S-F9 when the night raid hit. The men found Marek "Lucky" Mateorekon at dawn by the dugout door. Killed in the night raid by Dorian Royalcanadia of the Concord (@royalcanadianmatt).

Valentin "Whistle" Mateorekon had heard about Marek "Lucky" Mateorekon's courage. At S-F9, he also heard about the snoring, the cards and the terrible handwriting. As one of the first hundred volunteers, Valentin "Whistle" Mateorekon received the First Wave ribbon. A neighbour lent the needle and supervised every stitch. Orders came through: Valentin "Whistle" Mateorekon is a sniper now. He handed in his old kit and kept only a key to a house that is no longer there.

Valentin "Whistle" Mateorekon saw the glint of an enemy scope and fired first. The man behind it, Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks, was grazed. Valentin "Whistle" Mateorekon fired at the enemy dawn watch from S-F9. Walter Nightrunner was grazed, and the enemy line spent the morning with its heads down. Mail came up the line with a letter for Valentin "Whistle" Mateorekon. Valentin "Whistle" Mateorekon read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
raven_vader2026: Rafael Vader found a place in R-C2 between a snorer and a man who talked in his sleep. The available alternative was under the leak.
Day 10. Blackwater Canal fell to the Hegemony. Rafael Vader watched their flag go up on the heights and dug his trench a little deeper.

Rafael Vader began a chess game by post with a friend at home. He copied the opening move onto the corner of an ordinary letter. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Rafael Vader is number 780. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech.
s_mail6547: Quentin "Button" Mail introduced himself as a fisherman from Lindenbruck. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Quentin "Button" Mail wrote to twin brothers too young to enlist that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'

Quentin "Button" Mail carried Ivo "Smokes" Fox's rifle all the way up to Grey Mill after Smokes twisted an ankle. Neither has said thank you. Neither needs to. Quentin "Button" Mail got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 811. The men who came later will ask about it.
tephydraws: By the time Bram Tephydraws reached S-F5, the war was 2 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.
A replacement turned out to be from Stoneyford too. Bram Tephydraws and the newcomer argued about the same bakery for half the night.
Casimir Toro of the Hegemony and Bram Tephydraws of the Concord watched a broken branch near Verdel Ridge all morning. Neither could risk assuming it was only a branch.

Bram Tephydraws stood at the parapet at dawn with the rest of S-F5, bayonet fixed, staring into the grey. Nothing came. Nothing came yesterday, either. After the loss of Hill 304, Bram Tephydraws helped stack spare sandbags at S-F5. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
Bram Tephydraws's hands still remember being a coal miner's hands. Today they mended a broken duckboard as if it were the most important job in the world.
A round came through a gap in the sandbags at S-F5 and grazed Bram Tephydraws's arm. Two inches, the sergeant said. Shot by Benedikt "Smokes" Lfer of the Hegemony (@w0lfer2210).
The medic cut the last bandage off Bram Tephydraws's arm and threw it in the stove. He went back to S-F5 the same hour.
The aid post ran out of morphine at four. Bram Tephydraws held a boy's hand until six. Then he went back for the next one.
The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. Bram Tephydraws watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.

Bram Tephydraws drew a line on the bench to settle an argument about space. Everyone obeyed it until the broadest man returned from duty. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Bram Tephydraws answered to number 222.
vinnie2shoes: After 2 days of war, R-F6 had a place for everything. On Day 3, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Albin "Tin" Shoes.

Albin "Tin" Shoes transferred to the runners. The men in R-F6 said they would miss him. He is only three dugouts away. Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Albin "Tin" Shoes watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
Karel Pavla and Albin "Tin" Shoes compared drawings of home. Both drawings included a kitchen table larger than the house.

Albin "Tin" Shoes and Leopold "Brick" Moovin carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident. A letter from home reached Albin "Tin" Shoes before dusk. Albin "Tin" Shoes read it twice and slept a little easier.

A parcel came for Albin "Tin" Shoes that was really meant for another soldier with the same surname. Inside: several carefully wrapped biscuits. He put everything back and kept only the wrapping. A letter from home reached Albin "Tin" Shoes before dusk. Albin "Tin" Shoes read it twice and slept a little easier. The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Hill 304. Albin "Tin" Shoes read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.

Albin "Tin" Shoes and Yann Spring tried to invent a new card game. The rules only made sense once they stopped betting tobacco. A letter from home reached Albin "Tin" Shoes before dusk. Albin "Tin" Shoes read it twice and slept a little easier.

A round came through a gap in the sandbags at R-F6 and grazed Albin "Tin" Shoes's arm. Two inches, the sergeant said. Shot by Walter "Hollow" Malakaicripp of the Hegemony (@malakaicripps). A letter from home reached Albin "Tin" Shoes before dusk. Albin "Tin" Shoes read it twice and slept a little easier.
Albin "Tin" Shoes was carrying water up to R-F6 when a bullet hit him in the leg. The water reached the trench. Albin "Tin" Shoes did not. Shot by Gideon Bao of the Hegemony (@d4rth_bao).

Albin "Tin" Shoes lay on the stretcher and listened to the surgeon working inside. He tried not to guess what each sound meant. A letter from home reached Albin "Tin" Shoes before dusk. Albin "Tin" Shoes read it twice and slept a little easier.

Albin "Tin" Shoes spent a week on a stretcher in the corridor of the aid post. Today he stood up, held the wall, and walked out to R-F6. The Hegemony won Blackwater Canal. In R-F6, Albin "Tin" Shoes listened to three explanations and trusted none of them. A letter from home reached Albin "Tin" Shoes before dusk. Albin "Tin" Shoes read it twice and slept a little easier. Orders came through: Albin "Tin" Shoes is a signaller now. He handed in his old kit and kept only a stub of a pencil.

A parcel contained a bar of chocolate broken into uneven pieces. Albin "Tin" Shoes closed his eyes while someone else distributed them. Albin "Tin" Shoes got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 167. The men who came later will ask about it.
warwacko: The old hands of R-S11 have been here since Day 1. Lucien Warwacko has been here since Day 6. In a trench, that difference already feels like years.
Lucien Warwacko had Karel Adauto of the Concord in the sights at Saint-Ash crossroads for a long second. Karel Adauto was lighting a pipe. Lucien Warwacko let the match burn all the way down.

Somebody hung a doorbell on the next dugout. Lucien Warwacko went to look. It was a spoon tied to an empty tin. A letter from home reached Lucien Warwacko before dusk. Lucien Warwacko read it twice and slept a little easier.
A new trench junction cost Lucien Warwacko ten minutes. On the way back, he marked the right turn with a broken spoon.
Lucien Warwacko spent the night filling sandbags. By dawn he could no longer close his hands. By noon the shells had emptied half of them again.
On Day 10, Blackwater Canal passed to the Hegemony. Lucien Warwacko wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.

Lucien Warwacko took the long way round Calvary Farm because the short way had a sniper on it. The long way had two. The clerk counted the names twice. Lucien Warwacko is number 417 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand.
